beats.act: cold open
beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Divyank. You've built quizzes and flashcards from your chapters, but none of it means anything to a student until they can actually open it on a Monday morning. This chapter turns the book into a course package — and checks that the course a student sees still matches the plan you signed.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: Canvas has its own native course format. So does Moodle. So does Blackboard. A course package built to a shared standard runs on all of them — one track gauge, not three incompatible ones.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: An dot-I-M-S-C-C file is a ZIP archive with an X-M-L manifest inside it — a manifest that lists every page, module, quiz, and link, and tells any conforming system how to unpack them into a real course.

items: An XML manifest describing every resource
Pages, modules, quizzes, links — all addressed inside it
props.caption: a package, not a Canvas-specific format

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: The standard comes from 1EdTech — formerly IMS Global. The name changed in 2022, but the standard didn't restart. Current profile is version 1.3, and every importer still accepts the earlier versions too.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: A package addressed for one destination is a convenience. A package built to be sorted and delivered to any destination, by any carrier, is a standard — and that's the real difference between a Canvas export and a Common Cartridge.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: Build straight to Canvas's own A-P-I, and the course only ever lives in Canvas. Build to Common Cartridge instead, and Canvas becomes one of several places the exact same package can land.

beats.act: Act I — What You're Actually Exporting
beats.narration_text: Say it the way the chapter actually means it: this isn't export to Canvas. It's export to Canvas, or Moodle, or Blackboard, or whatever learning system you happen to be standing in front of.

beats.narration_text: One production line, run correctly, turns out the same kind of part every time. That's the whole design goal of this build step — one path in, one shape out, no matter which chapter set goes through it.

beats.narration_text: build-canvas-dot-s-h is a thin wrapper. The real work happens in build-imscc-standard-dot-p-y underneath it — and because every target goes through that one script, every package comes out shaped the same way.

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: Feed the same package into two different systems, and nothing about it changes to fit either one. The modules, the pages, the quizzes — they arrive the same, because the format never asked which platform it was headed for.

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: You can rename the file to dot-zip and open it like any archive. The manifest and the resource folders are sitting right there — worth doing once, so the whole format stops being a black box.

props.caption: worth doing once, so the format stops being a black box

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: What actually goes into the package is just the book's own shape, repackaged: chapters become pages, the quizzes you already generated become quiz objects, and the chapter order becomes the module order.

beats.act: Act II — One Command, One Path
beats.narration_text: One command, run against whichever target you point it at. That consistency is the entire reason the wrapper exists.

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: An import can finish without a single error and still hand you an empty room — a course that looks complete from the upload screen, with nothing behind its own doors.

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: Import it into a free Canvas teacher account, or any L-M-S you've got. The platform unpacks the manifest, and modules, pages, and quizzes populate the course — that's the import working as intended.

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: An import that throws no error can still fail completely. If the manifest never actually linked its resources, the course imports — and shows you nothing. No error message tells you which one just happened.

branches.label: Course looks empty

resolver.label: No error isn't the same as success

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: The fix starts with the manifest itself — inspect it, confirm the resources are actually linked inside it, and rebuild if they aren't. A package that imports but shows nothing failed silently, and the manifest is where that failure actually lives.

props.caption: a package that imports but shows nothing failed silently

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: The upload screen finishing without complaint was never the real test. Opening the imported course and actually looking at what's inside it is.

beats.act: Act III — Import, and the Silent Failure
beats.narration_text: If an import won't take at all, the chapter's own fixes are mechanical: confirm the package actually conforms, try a current importer, check the manifest directly.

beats.narration_text: One signed plan sequenced its modules Foundations, then Voice-of-Customer, then Offers, then Sales Page — establish, build, apply, in exactly that order.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Common Cartridge packages a course as a ZIP plus an X-M-L manifest — a shared standard, not a Canvas-specific format, importable by Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, and more. One command, one path: build-canvas-dot-s-h wraps build-imscc-standard-dot-p-y, so every target builds the same shape, and the package itself is never a black box. An import can finish without error and still fail — if the manifest never linked its resources, the course looks populated or looks empty, and only opening it tells you which. And module order carries real pedagogy: the only reliable check is against the signed plan, architecture-dot-m-d, not memory — a course imported alphabetically can look complete and still be wrong.
